names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 3 aprilie, «Sfântul Cuvios Nichita Mărturisitorul».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 3 Απριλίου, «Όσιος Νικήτας ο Ομολογητής Ηγούμενος Μονής Μηδικίου», with the rank word, the epithet and the office left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 3 April on pravoslavno.rs, „Св. Никита Исповедник“, with Св. left off — it is not a rank — and with the rank word Исповедник left off as well, which is what this folder's `confessor` carries. Medikion is in the body and not in the heading, so the heading gives no epithet at all and the bare forename is what the source gives.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 3 aprilie — «Sfântul Cuvios Nichita Mărturisitorul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 3ης Απριλίου — «Όσιος Νικήτας ο Ομολογητής Ηγούμενος Μονής Μηδικίου»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 3 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. It says «έζησε τον 8ο αιώνα μ.Χ.», that he lived in the eighth century, but its own narrative carries him past that: abbot under the patriarch Tarasios «(784 - 806 μ.Χ.)», exiled under Leo V «(813 - 820 μ.Χ.)» and again in 815, and back in Constantinople under Michael II the Stammerer «(820 - 829 μ.Χ.)», where he reposed. It gives no year for his death, so no dates are recorded from it here.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 16.04.2026 (3. април ст. ст.) — „Св. Никита Исповедник“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek already keep in this folder, and the same man beyond doubt: born at Caesarea in Bithynia; his father Philaretus taking the monastic habit after losing his wife, so that the boy was left with his grandmother; the monastery of Medikion, the abbot Nicephorus who tonsured him, the seven years before the patriarch Tarasius ordained him hieromonk, and the abbacy he took against his will after Nicephorus and his friend Athanasius died. **A death of 824 was added where this folder had none** — „Упокоји се овај велики јерарх 824. год.“ — and it is the only year any source read for this folder gives him. New to the folder besides that: the whole line of emperors, the devout Irene and the right-believing Nicephorus and Michael before Leo V the Armenian, under whom the iconoclast heresy flared again; the deposition of the patriarch Nicephorus and his exile, and the heretic Theodotus Cassiteras of unclean life raised in his place; the moving from prison to prison and the torments of hunger and thirst, frost and sweat and mockery; **the man named Nicholas who plagued him with jeering, until his own dead father appeared to him in a dream and told him to leave off the servant of God, after which he not only stopped but turned others from it**; the release of all the Orthodox sufferers when Leo died an evil death and the right-believing Michael Balbus took the empire; the solitary place near Constantinople where he spent his last days; the sick who touched his body at the funeral procession and were healed; and the relics laid beside those of his spiritual father Nicephorus and his friend Athanasius. **Nicholas and the father are not identified with anybody** — the entry gives neither a see, a monastery nor a by-name — and neither are the emperors or Theodotus, who take nothing. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion. The stored form Никита folds with `nicetas-the-chartularius` and `nicetas-the-goth`, which hold the same bare form; the fold is recorded as deliberate.

hymns.text: Cu curgerile lacrimilor tale ai lucrat pustiul cel neroditor şi cu suspinurile cele dintru adânc ai făcut ostenelile tale însutit roditoare; şi te-ai făcut luminător lumii, strălucind cu minunile, Nichita, părintele nostru. Roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu ca să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Nichita Mărturisitorul, egumenul Mănăstirii Midichiei, Glasul 8

english.text: With the streams of thy tears thou didst till the barren desert, and with sighs from the depths thou didst make thy labours bear fruit a hundredfold; and thou becamest a light to the world, shining with miracles, O Nicetas our father. Pray to Christ God that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Ὀρθοδοξίας ὁδηγέ, εὐσεβείας Διδάσκαλε καί σεμνότητος, τῆς Οἰκουμένης ὁ φωστήρ, τῶν Μοναζόντων θεόπνευστον ἐγκαλλώπισμα, Νικήτα σοφέ, ταῖς διδαχαῖς σου πάντας ἐφώτισας, λύρα τοῦ Πνεύματος. Πρέσβευε Χριστῷ τῷ Θεῷ, σωθῆναι τάς ψυχάς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr — Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’, on the page of Όσιος Νικήτας ο Ομολογητής Ηγούμενος Μονής Μηδικίου. This is the common apolytikion of a venerable confessor and teacher, with his name set into it; the page prints it first under his name, so it is copied whole as the page has it.

english.text: Guide of Orthodoxy, teacher of piety and of reverence, luminary of the world, God-inspired adornment of monastics, O wise Nicetas, by thy teachings thou hast enlightened all, O lyre of the Spirit. Intercede with Christ God that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Ὡς νίκης ἐπώνυμος τῶν θεοσδώτων θεσμῶν φρουρὸς ἀπερίτρεπτος καὶ στῦλος ὤφθης στερρός, Νικήτα μακάριε· σὺ γὰρ τῆς ἀπαθείας κοσμηθεὶς ταῖς ἀκτῖσιν αἴγλης ὁμολογίας τὸν σὸν βίον φαιδρύνεις. καὶ νῦν τῶν σοὶ προσιόντων δέχου τὴν αἴνεσιν.

source.text: saint.gr — Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε, on the page of Όσιος Νικήτας ο Ομολογητής Ηγούμενος Μονής Μηδικίου. It is his own and plays on his name, νίκης ἐπώνυμος, named for victory.

english.text: Named for victory, thou wast seen as an unturning guardian of the God-given ordinances and as a steadfast pillar, O blessed Nicetas; for adorned with the rays of dispassion thou dost make thy life bright with the splendour of confession. And now receive the praise of those who come to thee.

hymns.text: Ὡς ἡσυχίας ὑποφήτης, πρακτικώτατος, τῆς ποιμανσίας ὀφθαλμός ὤφθης ἀκοίμητος τῆς Μονῆς καθηγησάμενος Μηδικίου· Ἀλλ᾽ὡς φύλαξ τῶν ἐνθέων παραδόσεων διαρρύθμισον Νικήτα θείῳ Πνεύματι τοὺς βοῶντάς σοι, χαίροις Πάτερ τρισόλβιε.

source.text: saint.gr — Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’, Τῇ ὑπερμάχῳ, on the page of Όσιος Νικήτας ο Ομολογητής Ηγούμενος Μονής Μηδικίου. It names him and names his monastery, Μηδικίου.

english.text: As a most practised interpreter of stillness, thou wast seen to be a sleepless eye of the shepherd's charge, having led the monastery of Medikion. But as a guardian of the God-filled traditions, set in order by the divine Spirit, O Nicetas, those who cry to thee: Rejoice, thrice-blessed Father.

death.note: The Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the Julian 3 April: „Упокоји се овај велики јерарх 824. год.“ — this great hierarch reposed in the year 824. It is the only year any source read for this folder gives him; neither doxologia.ro's life nor saint.gr's prints one, and the reigns they name — Leo V the Armenian, then Michael Balbus — are consistent with it. `node .tmp/dd.mjs 824` reads in Russian and Greek.
